title: Pastebin: Text Snippet Sharing
summary: Design a service where people paste text or code, share it through an unguessable link, and optionally have it expire or self-destruct after the first view.
statement:
You are designing **a paste-sharing service**: developers paste a log excerpt, a config file or a code snippet and share the link in a chat or a bug report.

**Users**
- *Anonymous users* can create pastes and view any public or unlisted paste whose link they have.
- *Registered users* can also create private pastes (only they can view them), list their own pastes and delete them.

**Core journeys**
1. **Create** — submit text (up to 10 MB) with an optional title, a syntax-language hint, a visibility (public, unlisted or private) and an expiry (10 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day, 1 week, 1 month or never). The service returns a short, unguessable link such as `https://paste.example/kq81Lz0w`.
2. **View** — opening the link shows the paste and its metadata. A "raw" link returns only the plain text; scripts and CI jobs fetch raw links a lot.
3. **Burn after reading** — a paste can be marked so that exactly one person can ever view it; after the first successful view it is gone for everyone.
4. **Manage** — registered users see a paginated list of their pastes and can delete any of them.
5. **Recent** — a public page lists the 50 newest public pastes.

**Clarifications from the interviewer**
- Pastes are immutable once created; there is no editing (people create a new paste instead).
- Expired or deleted pastes must stop being viewable promptly — within about a minute — even if the underlying storage is cleaned up later.
- Most pastes are small (median ~5 KB), but a meaningful minority are multi-megabyte log dumps.
- A paste linked from a busy forum thread or an outage post-mortem can get thousands of views per minute.

Cover requirements, estimates, APIs, the data model and the high-level architecture, then dive into the parts you consider most interesting.
scaleHints: 5M new pastes per day (~60 creations/s on average, ~300/s at peak)
Read:write about 10:1 → ~50M views per day (~600/s on average, ~3K/s at peak)
Average paste 10 KB (median 5 KB, maximum 10 MB) → ~50 GB of new content per day
About half of all pastes never expire; plan for 3 years of growth (~55 TB of content if nothing expired)
View latency p99 under 200 ms for pastes up to 1 MB
constraints: Links must be unguessable — unlisted pastes are protected only by nobody being able to discover the link
A burn-after-reading paste must be shown to at most one viewer, even if two people open it at the same moment
Once the creator has received the link, the paste must not be lost
Creation must be limited per client to stop abuse (e.g. 100 pastes per hour for anonymous clients)
outOfScope: Editing pastes, forks and revision history
Syntax highlighting itself (done in the browser)
Comments, stars and other social features

keyFunctionalRequirements: Create a paste with content, optional title, language, visibility and expiry; return a unique link
View rendered and raw paste by key; enforce visibility for private pastes
Expiry: expired pastes are never served; physical cleanup happens asynchronously
Burn after reading with exactly-one-view semantics
Registered users list (paginated) and delete their pastes
Recent public pastes list bounded to the newest 50
keyNonFunctionalRequirements: Read-heavy (10:1) with ~3K views/s at peak and bursty hot pastes
Low view latency (p99 < 200 ms for pastes up to 1 MB)
Large 10 MB payloads must not degrade small-paste performance
Cost-efficient storage over years (~55 TB worst case), e.g. compression and tiering
Abuse protection through per-client rate and size limits
coreEntities: PasteMetadata: paste_key (PK), owner_id, title, language, visibility, size_bytes, content_ref, created_at, expires_at, burn_after_read, status
PasteContent: immutable blob addressed by content_ref
RecentPublic: bounded list of (created_at, paste_key) for the newest public pastes
keyComponents: Stateless API/web tier for create, view, raw and list
Key generation with enough entropy (random keys + collision check, or a pre-generated key pool)
Metadata store keyed by paste_key with a secondary index on owner_id for listings
Object/blob storage for paste content, separate from metadata
Cache for hot pastes (immutability makes caching simple) and edge caching of public raw content
Expiry: read-time check plus a background cleanup worker
deepDiveTopics: Separating metadata from content: blobs in object storage vs inline rows, and a size threshold for small pastes
Burn after reading: an atomic state transition (active → burned) before returning content, and keeping caches from serving it
Expiry: lazy check on read plus background deletion; cache TTLs bounded by expires_at
Key length and entropy so unlisted and private links cannot be guessed or enumerated
Serving popular and raw pastes cheaply by caching immutable content, without exposing private pastes
commonPitfalls: Storing multi-megabyte bodies in relational rows and loading them for listings
Relying only on a periodic cleanup job, so expired pastes stay visible for hours
Read-then-delete for burn after reading, letting two concurrent viewers both see the paste
Short sequential keys that make unlisted pastes enumerable
Caching private or burn-after-reading pastes in a shared cache layer
